OPEN SOURCE

Open source contributions.

Upstream fixes for SDK reliability and evaluation accuracy. Each pull request explains what broke and what the proposed fix changes.

OPEN PULL REQUESTS

8 pull requests in 3 repositories
  • openai/evals #1861
    OpenNov 2026

    The JSON Patch benchmark could reject valid answers based on formatting and accept invalid answers that contained the expected text.

    Compares parsed JSON and accepts equivalent patch operations, so formatting does not affect the score.

  • modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk #1471
    OpenNov 2026

    Oversized requests sent over standard input could be silently dropped, leaving callers waiting for a timeout.

    Returns an explicit error tied to the request ID when that ID can be safely recovered.

  • openai/evals #1860
    OpenNov 2026

    A polynomial benchmark had incorrect reference answers for 301 of its 500 cases.

    Corrects the root-count labels using exact arithmetic and preserves the original dataset version for comparison.

  • anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python #2073
    OpenNov 2026

    A session runner could execute pending tools after reconnecting to a session that had already ended.

    Checks for session termination in history before dispatching tools, then closes the stream and exits.

  • anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python #2072
    OpenNov 2026

    One-shot tool iterators could be emptied when the SDK retried a rejected thread request.

    Keeps the same tool definitions across recovery attempts in both sync and async clients.

  • anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python #2071
    OpenNov 2026

    Cancelling an async poller could leave acknowledged work running and its trace open.

    Lets graceful shutdown finish during cancellation and always closes the work span.

  • anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python #2070
    OpenNov 2026

    Queued messages could push a tool result out of order and make the next API request invalid.

    Places each tool result immediately after the model reply that requested it.

  • anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python #2069
    OpenNov 2026

    Reopening an async stream manager reused an already-awaited coroutine and failed.

    Opens a fresh stream on each entry and prevents older streams from ending the current turn.
